alt: A ladder of five sizes running from a colonic crypt a few hundred micrometres long down to the 2 nm width of the DNA double helix, with the limit of unaided vision between the crypt and one crypt cell, and the light-microscope limit below the cell.
longDescription: Five rungs, largest at the top. Rung one: one colonic crypt, a tube of roughly 700 cells stacked about 32 along its length, so its length is a few hundred micrometres. Rung two: the finest detail the unaided eye separates, about 0.1 mm, which is 100 micrometres. Rung three: one colonic epithelial cell, about 10 to 20 micrometres across. Rung four: the finest detail a conventional light microscope separates, about 0.25 micrometres, which is 250 nanometres. Rung five: the DNA double helix, about 2 nanometres across. Each threshold sits between the two structures it separates. The crypt is roughly three to six times larger than the eye's threshold, so a crypt opening is at the edge of what an unaided eye could resolve, while a cell is five to ten times smaller than that same threshold, which is the gap a lens had to close before anyone could see that tissue is built from cells. Lower down, one crypt cell is about a thirtieth of the whole crypt's length; a crypt cell is about forty to eighty times wider than the light microscope's limit, so a lens shows it easily; and the light-microscope limit is about a hundred times wider than the DNA helix, so no light microscope shows the helix at all.
